tldr: No moves from Simplii's direct Canadian competitors today. The one Canadian bank item is an RBC Insurance group-benefits launch, which is not relevant to Simplii. The useful signals come from exchanges and fintechs: low-minimum global ETFs, extended trading hours, tokenized stocks, and new payment rails. Mercado Bitcoin's fee change is a notable pricing move.
themes: Low-minimum, fractional-style access to global ETFs
Fee restructuring and removing funding options
Premium card points and travel-perk arms race

highlights.headline: Itaú launched a Vanguard-linked global stock ETF covering about 98% of global equities, with investments starting at R$50 (about C$13).
highlights.why: A bank packaging a one-click global equity ETF at a tiny entry point resets expectations for low-minimum, diversified investing. Simplii's investing and self-directed offering should be benchmarked against this.

highlights.headline: Nasdaq published a 23/5 trading information hub, and OKX and ICE (NYSE's parent) are launching a tokenized-stock venue with 113 assets lined up.
highlights.why: Near-around-the-clock and tokenized equity trading is moving from concept to infrastructure. Simplii should decide on its position on extended-hours trading before customers start asking for it.

highlights.headline: Klarna is now payable inside Adyen's agentic AI checkout, and Mercado Pago launched 'Quick Payments' for buying without presenting a card.
highlights.why: Payments are moving toward agent-driven and card-free flows. This could change how Simplii's debit and credit products show up at checkout, so tokenization and wallet readiness matter.

highlights.headline: Mercado Bitcoin will charge every customer a R$46.80 annual fee in place of its inactivity fee. Separately, Mercado Pago is ending debit-card top-ups from December.
highlights.why: Both moves show platforms restructuring fees and funding options. As a no-fee, low-cost brand, Simplii can use this as a differentiation point. It also shows how a change to funding methods lands with customers.
